M1_dvol_meanrev.name: DVOL shock -> own forward change (vol-of-vol mean reversion)
M1_dvol_meanrev.hypothesis: A DVOL spike today mean-reverts tomorrow: d_dvol(t) negatively predicts d_dvol(t+1..3), a timing signal for short-variance entries distinct from A14 (which used DVOL shock to forecast underlying RV, not DVOL itself).
M1_dvol_meanrev.notes: No execution vehicle in this dataset (would need to trade DVOL/variance swaps directly, not present).

M2_rv_iv_spread.name: RV-IV spread level -> own mean reversion / forward RV
M2_rv_iv_spread.hypothesis: The gap between ATM IV and trailing realized vol (the current variance-risk-premium level) mean-reverts, and/or predicts forward RV directly -- distinct from A14 which used IV SHOCKS, not the level of the RV-IV gap, and did not test the spreads own dynamics.
M2_rv_iv_spread.notes: CONFOUND CHECKED, SURVIVES (partially): raw IC -0.64 is largely mechanical -- spread(t)=atm_iv(t)-sameday_rv(t) is dominated by sameday_rv (IV moves far less day-to-day than realized vol does), so spread(t) is close to -sameday_rv(t) in disguise, and the near-identical baseline "-sameday_rv(t) alone -> spread_fwd_change3d" IC (-0.568 vs raw -0.643) confirms most of the raw number is just RV mean-reversion relabeled. BUT after formally partialling out sameday_rv(t) (rank-residualized), a large incremental partial IC of -0.388 (n=1291, p<1e-16) remains -- stronger survival than A14s own confound-passing threshold (+0.224 partial). Sign-stable across both time-split halves (-0.672 / -0.627 raw). This IS the VOL_RISK_PREMIUM mechanism from reports/options/VOL_RISK_PREMIUM.md (that report established the premium EXISTS unconditionally); this test adds that the spreads day-to-day level, even net of same-day RV clustering, still carries real incremental timing information for its own forward change -- a genuinely new, confound-checked result, not just a relabeling of RV clustering.

M3_block_flow_returns.name: Block-trade net flow -> forward perp returns (daily)
M3_block_flow_returns.hypothesis: Deribit block trades (institutional execution channel, is_block=True) carry directional information: net bullish block flow predicts BTC perp appreciation. Distinct from the closed OPTIONS_POSITIONING_4H protocol (NO_EDGE_DEFINITIF) which used ALL flow (not block-restricted) at 4h buckets with z-score normalization; here restricted to the institutional block channel at daily horizon, raw and z-scored.

M4_large_nonblock_flow_returns.name: Large non-block trade flow -> forward perp returns (daily)
M4_large_nonblock_flow_returns.hypothesis: Large trades that do NOT clear the official Deribit block threshold (top-5%-by-notional of the days non-block trades) still carry informed directional flow, comparable to but distinct from the official block channel (M3).
M4_large_nonblock_flow_returns.data_source: trades/BTC (large non-block subset, notional >= days 95th pct)

M5_block_activity_rv.name: Block-trade activity level -> forward realized vol
M5_block_activity_rv.hypothesis: Days with unusually high block-trade activity (count/notional, not directional sign) precede higher realized vol -- distinct from A14s block_share (a SHARE-of-total metric already tested with IC -0.13/-0.19 on rv_fwd3) since this uses raw activity level/count, not share-of-volume.
M5_block_activity_rv.metric: Spearman IC + confound-controlled partial IC vs sameday_rv

M6_otm_put_tailhedge.name: Far-OTM put activity share -> forward RV (crash-hedging demand)
M6_otm_put_tailhedge.hypothesis: The share of daily options notional concentrated in far-OTM puts (strike <= 0.85x spot) is a tail-hedging-demand gauge; rising demand for crash protection should precede realized-vol expansion. Distinct from top_strike_share (ATM concentration) already tested in A14.
M6_otm_put_tailhedge.metric: Spearman IC + confound-controlled partial IC vs sameday_rv

M7_term_structure_level.name: Term-structure slope (near-30d ATM IV minus far-90/180d ATM IV) -> forward RV/returns
M7_term_structure_level.hypothesis: Backwardation (near IV > far IV, i.e. term_slope>0) signals near-term stress and should precede higher realized vol; contango (term_slope<0) signals calm. Trade-flow-implied, NOT OI-weighted (explicitly flagged: this is median trade-IV per expiry bucket, not a true OI-weighted surface).
M7_term_structure_level.data_source: trades/BTC ATM band (|log_moneyness|<=0.05), split by days_to_expiry <=30 vs 60-180
M7_term_structure_level.metric: Spearman IC + confound-controlled partial IC vs sameday_rv

M8_cross_expiry_relative_change.name: Near-expiry IV move vs far-expiry IV move (divergence) -> forward RV
M8_cross_expiry_relative_change.hypothesis: When near-dated IV moves MORE than far-dated IV on the same day (term structure steepening shock), that divergence itself -- not the shock in either leg alone -- predicts forward RV. A term-structure-specific RV trade, distinct from A14s single-IV shock and from M7s level test.
M8_cross_expiry_relative_change.metric: Spearman IC + confound-controlled partial IC vs sameday_rv

M9_expiry_proximity.name: Monthly-expiry-proximity effect on realized vol / ATM IV (pinning & crush, no OI)
M9_expiry_proximity.hypothesis: As BTC approaches DERIBITS STANDARD MONTHLY expiry (last Friday of month, 08:00 UTC -- pure calendar convention, not data-dependent), does same-day realized vol or ATM IV level/crush differ from non-expiry days? A true pin-risk/max-pain measure would need OI (SKIPPED, absent from this dataset); this tests the calendar-proximity effect only.
M9_expiry_proximity.data_source: trades/BTC ATM band joined to a hardcoded Deribit monthly-expiry calendar (last Friday/month)
M9_expiry_proximity.metric: Kruskal-Wallis across days-to-next-monthly-expiry buckets (same-day RV) + IC(days_to_expiry -> atm_iv level)

time_split_stability.note: cross-sectional bucket test, not a chronological split

M10_iv_regime_transition.name: IV regime SWITCH (tercile low/mid/high) -> forward RV/returns
M10_iv_regime_transition.hypothesis: A regime TRANSITION (e.g. jumping from the bottom IV tercile straight to the top) carries different forward-RV information than persisting in the same regime or than the magnitude of a single-day shock (A14s construction) -- distinct signal: discreteness of the switch itself.
M10_iv_regime_transition.data_source: features/BTC_daily.parquet atm_iv terciles (90-day-lookback-free, whole-sample qcut for discovery purposes -- flagged as in-sample tercile cutoffs, a caveat for live use)
M10_iv_regime_transition.metric: Mann-Whitney U, switch cohorts vs no-switch cohort on rv_fwd3d

M11_btc_move_iv_repricing.name: BTC move -> next-day IV repricing (leverage effect + magnitude), and does repricing mean-revert
M11_btc_move_iv_repricing.hypothesis: Reverse causality, three sub-tests: (a) leverage effect -- does a signed down-move raise next-day ATM IV more than an up-move of the same size (classic equity-style leverage effect, untested for this crypto options market at daily granularity); (b) magnitude -- does |move| predict |repricing| regardless of sign; (c) conditional on the top-decile biggest-move days specifically, does the resulting IV repricing then reverse the following day (overreaction fade, a short-vol-after-spike timing trade).
M11_btc_move_iv_repricing.data_source: trades/BTC ATM band + Binance perp same-day return

M12_cumulative_flow_momentum.name: Rolling 3d/7d cumulative options flow -> forward returns/RV (positioning momentum)
M12_cumulative_flow_momentum.hypothesis: Sustained multi-day options positioning buildup (not a single-day flow reading, which is the closed OPTIONS_POSITIONING_4H protocols construction) predicts subsequent perp direction or vol -- a momentum/persistence variant rather than an instantaneous-flow variant.
M12_cumulative_flow_momentum.data_source: trades/BTC, 3d/7d rolling sums of net_flow_all and block_flow

M13_options_flow_basis.name: Options net flow -> forward perp basis/premium change (Binance)
M13_options_flow_basis.hypothesis: Aggregate bullish/bearish options flow on Deribit predicts subsequent widening/narrowing of the Binance BTCUSDT perp premium (a basis proxy) the next day -- tests whether options positioning leaks into a DIFFERENT venues funding-adjacent pricing, not perp returns directly.
M13_options_flow_basis.notes: Deribit (options) and Binance (premium) are different venues/clocks; joined on UTC calendar day with same-day mean premium, forward = next calendar days mean, so alignment tolerance is coarse (day-level) by construction -- flagged per hard rule 7.

M14_dvol_shock_returns.name: DVOL shock -> forward perp DIRECTIONAL returns
M14_dvol_shock_returns.hypothesis: A14 used DVOL shocks to forecast realized VOL (IC +0.128/+0.148). Here the same DVOL-shock signal is tested against DIRECTIONAL forward returns instead -- does a vol-index spike itself carry directional information (e.g. vol spikes cluster with down moves)?

M15_pc_ratio_level_rv.name: Put/call volume ratio LEVEL (not day-over-day delta) -> forward RV
M15_pc_ratio_level_rv.hypothesis: The absolute LEVEL of put/call volume ratio (a standing positioning-skew gauge) predicts forward RV, distinct from A14 (which used the day-over-day DELTA of related flow fields for RV forecasting) and distinct from the closed positioning protocol (which targeted returns, not RV, and used deltas).
M15_pc_ratio_level_rv.metric: Spearman IC + confound-controlled partial IC vs sameday_rv

M16_hourly_iv_shock.name: Hourly ATM-IV shock (trade-implied) -> next-hour perp return/RV
M16_hourly_iv_shock.hypothesis: A14s hourly test used flow variables (notional_z, n_block, block_share_hr, cp_imbalance) to forecast next-hour |return|. This tests the hourly IV-LEVEL SHOCK itself (d_atm_iv within the hour), which A14 did not test at hourly granularity (only daily d_atm_iv_traded).
M16_hourly_iv_shock.notes: Very sparse per-hour ATM trade counts (median likely <10) -- flagged as a data-density caveat.

M17_hourly_block_longer_rv.name: Hourly block-trade count/notional -> forward RV at 4h/24h (longer horizon than A14 hourly)
M17_hourly_block_longer_rv.hypothesis: A14s hourly test forecast 1h forward |return| using notional_z/n_block. This tests whether the same hourly block-trade signal has predictive power at LONGER RV horizons (4h, 24h) -- does the block-flow information decay fast (pure microstructure) or persist (genuine information)?
M17_hourly_block_longer_rv.metric: Spearman IC + confound-controlled partial IC vs trailing 24h RV
